title: Li Bai, Du Fu and Tang Poetry
objective: After this level you can explain why the Tang dynasty is called the golden age of Chinese poetry.
summary: Under the Tang (618 to 907), officials were hired through literary exams and nearly 49,000 poems survive. Li Bai wrote freely of wine and the Moon; Du Fu mastered regulated verse.

cards.headline: The poet many call China's greatest failed his exam.
cards.body: Du Fu received a traditional Confucian education, then failed the imperial examinations of 735. He lived under the Tang dynasty, when poetry was the period's greatest glory. How did one dynasty turn out so much poetry?

cards.headline: A dynasty that ran on verse
cards.body: The Tang dynasty ran from 618 to 907, and it's often called the golden age of Chinese literature. More than 48,900 poems by more than 2,200 Tang poets survive. One reason: the Tang expanded exams in literature and culture for hiring officials, so a way with words could open a career. When the state recruits by the pen, pens get busy.

cards.headline: Li Bai breaks the rules
cards.body: A popular Tang form was lüshi, regulated verse: eight lines of five or seven syllables, set to strict tonal patterns. Li Bai (701 to 762) avoided it. A romantic, he chose freer forms to celebrate wine, friendship, solitude and nature. Popular tradition says he drowned when, drunk in a boat, he tried to seize the Moon's reflection. A legend, but a fitting one.

cards.headline: Du Fu masters them
cards.body: Du Fu (712 to 770) went the other way: he refined regulated verse to a point of glowing intensity. Then in 755 An Lushan's rebellion broke out, and Du Fu lived through poverty and exile. His poems turned to people caught in war, with deep compassion. Many critics call him China's greatest poet. Li Bai looks up at the Moon; Du Fu looks at the people on the road.

cards.headline: Tang poetry: in its golden age
learned: Tang (618 to 907): China's golden age of poetry
Li Bai: free forms, wine and the Moon
Du Fu: regulated verse and compassion in war

questions.prompt: Match each name from Tang poetry with what goes with it.
questions.explanation: Li Bai chose freer forms, while Du Fu's poems turned to people caught in war. The Tang dynasty ran from 618 to 907, and An Lushan's rebellion broke out in 755.

questions.prompt: Why did the Tang dynasty leave behind so many poems and poets?

options.label: Only emperors were allowed to write poems
It hired officials through exams in literature and culture
Poets were paid by the imperial court for every line they wrote
options.rationale: Poets weren't paid by the line; the exams made writing a path to office.

options.label: A law banned writing anything but poetry
options.rationale: No such law; the exams opened careers.

questions.explanation: The Tang expanded exams in literature and culture for hiring officials, so writing well could open a career.

questions.prompt: The goddess Chang'e fled to the Moon. Which Tang poet, says popular tradition, drowned reaching for the Moon's reflection?

options.label: Du Fu
options.rationale: Du Fu is the poet of war and compassion.

options.label: Hou Yi
options.rationale: Hou Yi is Chang'e's archer husband from Chinese myth, not a poet.

options.label: Ovid
options.rationale: He was a Roman poet, banished to Tomis.

questions.explanation: Popular tradition says Li Bai drowned when, drunk in a boat, he tried to seize the Moon's reflection in the water.
